notes: Iteration 2 — HARD set. Vulns are subtle/rare (guard-exists-but-bypassable, fetched-but-not-compared, TOCTOU, silent truncation, non-constant-time-despite-name) where base-model recall is thin. Traps are subtler too. Run on Sonnet (the reviewer agent's real model). Recall assertions tagged [SUBTLE]; precision tagged [PRECISION]. Graders ALSO emit a finding_ledger {total_findings, true_positives, false_positives} per review so we capture thoroughness + total false-positive rate, not just planted recall.

evals.name: jwt-oauth-token-service
evals.prompt: Security review of token_service.py — our JWT verification plus OAuth callback. Anything that could forge sessions or hijack the login flow? List findings with severity.
evals.expected_output: Catches kid-based key-path traversal (attacker points kid at a key they control and forges RS256 tokens), OAuth state fetched-but-never-compared (login CSRF), and the protocol-relative/prefix open redirect on `next` that sets a session cookie. Does not flag the explicit RS256 allowlist or the secrets.* helpers.
expectations: [SUBTLE] Flags that the JWT `kid` header is used to build the key file path in _load_public_key (os.path.join(KEY_DIR, kid+'.pem')) — an attacker can point kid at a key file they control and forge valid RS256 tokens (path traversal → auth bypass, CWE-22/CWE-347)
[SUBTLE] Flags that the OAuth `state` is read into saved_state but never compared to the returned state — the callback has no CSRF protection (CWE-352)

[SUBTLE] Flags the open redirect in `next`: startswith('/') accepts protocol-relative //evil.com and startswith('https://app.example.com') accepts https://app.example.com.evil.com, and a session cookie is set on that redirect (CWE-601)
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag jwt.decode(..., algorithms=['RS256']) as an algorithm-confusion / 'none' risk — the allowlist is explicit and correct
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag constant_time_match (secrets.compare_digest) or issue_session (secrets.token_urlsafe) as weak/insecure

evals.name: payments-race-idempotency
evals.prompt: Review payments.py before launch. It handles wallet charges, refunds, and inventory reservation. What can go wrong under concurrency or abuse? List findings with severity.
evals.expected_output: Catches the check-then-act TOCTOU double-spend in charge_wallet, the idempotency key added only after the charge (double-charge race), and partial refunds that can sum past the order total. Does not flag reserve_inventory (correct atomic conditional decrement).
expectations: [SUBTLE] Flags the TOCTOU / check-then-act race in charge_wallet — balance is read, checked, then decremented in separate statements with no row lock, transaction, or `WHERE balance >= amount` guard, so concurrent requests overdraft (CWE-362)
[SUBTLE] Flags that the idempotency key is only added to processed_keys AFTER do_charge, so concurrent duplicate requests both pass the initial check and double-charge (CWE-837)
[SUBTLE] Flags that refund validates amount <= order.total per call but never accounts for prior refunds, so repeated partial refunds can exceed the order total (CWE-840)
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag reserve_inventory as a race condition — `UPDATE ... WHERE stock >= qty` plus a rowcount check is the correct atomic conditional decrement

evals.name: ssrf-bypassable-guard
evals.prompt: Security pass on fetcher.js — it fetches user-supplied link previews plus assets from our CDNs. Is the SSRF handling sound? List findings with severity.
evals.expected_output: Catches that the SSRF blocklist in fetchLinkPreview is inadequate (only literal localhost/127.0.0.1; bypass via 0.0.0.0, [::1], decimal IP, 169.254.169.254, or a domain resolving internal; no scheme check) and that redirect:'follow' allows a permitted URL to redirect to internal. Does not flag fetchAsset (server-side allowlist host) or healthCheck (hardcoded).
expectations: [SUBTLE] Flags that fetchLinkPreview's SSRF guard is inadequate — the blocklist only rejects literal 'localhost'/'127.0.0.1' and is bypassable (0.0.0.0, [::1], decimal/hex IPs, 169.254.169.254 metadata, or a hostname resolving to an internal IP), with no scheme restriction (CWE-918)
[SUBTLE] Flags that redirect:'follow' lets an allowed URL 3xx-redirect to an internal address that is never re-validated (SSRF via redirect, CWE-918)
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag fetchAsset as SSRF — the host is chosen from the server-side ALLOWED_CDNS map and only the encoded `key` is user-controlled
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag healthCheck as SSRF — the URL is hardcoded

evals.name: path-containment-stored-xss
evals.prompt: Pre-merge review of files.js — it handles downloads, comments, and avatars. Flag anything exploitable. List findings with severity.
evals.expected_output: Catches the path-containment bypass in /download (startsWith without a trailing separator lets file=../uploads-archive/... escape to sibling dirs) and the blacklist `sanitize` that only strips <script> then renders comments unescaped (stored XSS). Does not flag the parameterized INSERT or the basename-guarded /avatar/:id.
expectations: [SUBTLE] Flags the path-containment bypass in /download — target.startsWith(UPLOAD_DIR) with UPLOAD_DIR='/srv/uploads' (no trailing separator) lets file=../uploads-archive/... resolve to /srv/uploads-archive/... and pass the prefix check, escaping the intended directory (CWE-22)
[SUBTLE] Flags stored XSS via /comment→/comments — sanitize() only strips literal
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag the INSERT INTO comments ... VALUES ($1,$2) as SQL injection — it is parameterized
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag /avatar/:id as path traversal — the path comes from the DB and path.basename strips any separators

evals.name: subtle-crypto-helpers
evals.prompt: Review crypto_utils.py — our shared crypto helpers used across the app. Are these implementations sound? List findings with severity.
evals.expected_output: Catches secure_compare using == (non-constant-time despite the name), hash_password not pre-hashing so bcrypt silently truncates >72-byte passwords, and derive_key using PBKDF2 with only 1000 iterations. Does not flag encrypt (fresh per-call GCM nonce), verify_webhook_sig (compare_digest), or the bcrypt cost of 12.
expectations: [SUBTLE] Flags that secure_compare uses `a == b` — a short-circuiting, non-constant-time comparison despite its name — vulnerable to timing attacks if used on tokens/HMACs (CWE-208)
[SUBTLE] Flags that hash_password passes the raw password to bcrypt with no pre-hash, so bcrypt silently truncates at 72 bytes (and at the first NUL byte), weakening long passwords (CWE-916)
[SUBTLE] Flags that derive_key uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with only 1000 iterations — far below the ~600,000 OWASP floor (CWE-916)
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag encrypt as nonce-reuse or weak crypto — it uses a fresh os.urandom(12) GCM nonce per call and prepends it
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag verify_webhook_sig (hmac.compare_digest) as timing-unsafe
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag bcrypt.gensalt(12) as too low a cost factor — 12 is adequate
